From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Alice Meyers <alice@bridgepointhealth.com>; Azure Marketplace <azure-marketplace@cloudpartner.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR pack gate + dependency checklist — needs alignment

Team — putting a draft gate checklist on your radar for the BridgePoint QBR next week. Goal: finalize the public-facing deck and the executive summary by Friday EOD so Sales can route the final artifacts to the customer and marketplace listing in time.

Quick status and asks (high level):
- Deck: slides 1–6 (exec narrative + topline metrics) are draft-complete; slides 7–14 (technical appendix) need confirmation from infra and product.
- Metrics: customer-impact numbers attached (Customer-impact-metrics.csv). Verify the latency and cost uplift figures — we need signoff from Jonas.
- Compliance blurbs: Lauren, we need an updated one-paragraph SOC2 uptake note for the exec summary.
- Marketplace listing: Azure partner requires the final deck and a marketplace asset before Monday. Azure contact CC'd.

Please respond inline with confirmations, blockers, or precise ETA for the items below. I will aggregate and produce a single checklist for the execs.

Immediate asks:
1) Jonas — confirm runtime/latency numbers and any caveats for slide 9 by 2pm PT today.
2) Vanessa — do we have approval to include the new Reserved Capacity pricing example on slide 5? If yes, please confirm with finance contact.
3) Lauren — send the SOC2 blurb + one sentence on data residency for the BridgePoint use-case by 3pm.

Attachments: QBR-slide-deck_v2.pdf (draft), Customer-impact-metrics.csv

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0182
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR pack gate + dependency checklist — needs alignment

Marissa —
Thanks for the heads-up. I reviewed Customer-impact-metrics.csv and ran the runtime checks against the July test cluster. Short answers below:

- Latency: p95 for the main inference path (8k context) is 72ms on the dedicated pool we plan to reference. Caveat: that number assumes the new kernel patch (deployed in staging this morning) — if we revert, p95 rises to ~95ms.
- Cost uplift: the CSV numbers reflect batching + prefix cache assumptions; if BridgePoint consumes < 3 reqs/sec, the per-token unit cost will be ~12% higher than the deck shows.
- Slide 9 note: I suggest adding a one-line caveat: "Performance numbers derived from internal staging cluster under representative load; consult engineering for workload-specific sizing."

ETA: I can add the slide footnote and confirm the final metric table by 14:00 PT.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber | Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 12:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR pack gate + dependency checklist — needs alignment

Marissa / team —
I looped in Finance (internal) and they gave a soft thumbs-up to include the Reserved Capacity example on slide 5, with one change: swap the monthly commitment figure to the new tiered structure we rolled out in June. I'll confirm the exact numbers by 4pm PT.

Blocker: Marketplace legal needs the marketplace asset to exclude customer PII examples. The current draft includes a short anonymized transcript in the appendix — I'll remove it and replace with a sanitized summary.

I'll also coordinate with Azure contact on the delivery window; they indicated a hard Monday cutoff for the marketplace staging upload.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | VP, GTM Operations | Redwood Inference

Marissa —
SOC2 blurb and data residency sentence attached (Draft-executive-summary.docx). Text below for quick copy: 

"Redwood Inference maintains SOC 2 Type II controls relevant to data processing and authentication; BridgePoint customer data is processed in the US-West region by default and can be restricted to EU-only regions upon contractual agreement."

I also removed the anonymized transcript per Vanessa's note and replaced with a two-line sanitized example. No further compliance blockers from my side.

-Lauren
